From: Lucas Perry <lucas@cascade.ai>

Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected missing answers from Redwood endpoint

Hi Hannah,

We're seeing intermittent calls to the Redwood generation endpoint return an empty body (200 OK, zero-length text) — roughly 2/10 calls for the same prompt batch. This started Friday afternoon PST and has impacted a small production workflow (not all customers).

I've attached a screenshot and a small API sample with request IDs we captured. Sample request ids: req_5f9c2a, req_5f9c2b, req_5f9c2d. We're using the official Redwood JS SDK (v1.3.0) and hitting the hosted API in us-west-2. No client-side errors in our logs other than empty response parsing failures.

Can you triage whether this looks like a platform issue? We rely on predictable outputs and this is affecting a job in production.

Attachments: screencap_20260810.png (image/png), api_sample_60810.txt (text/plain)

Thanks,
Lucas
Senior SRE, CascadeAI

Hi Lucas — thanks for the report and for including request ids and the screenshot. We'll prioritize a triage. A few quick asks to help speed root cause:

- Can you confirm the SDK version (you noted v1.3.0) and whether you are using any custom proxy or retry logic?
- Do you have a stable repro script we can run, or are the empty responses intermittent across different payloads?

I'm looping in our on-call support and engineering to reproduce. We'll update within 24h and share any server-side logs that might correlate.

— Hannah

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:10:30 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Unexpected missing answers from Redwood endpoint (CascadeAI) — triage findings

Quick update after reproducing with the customer's sample:

What I did
- Replayed their api_sample_60810.txt payloads against the hosted endpoint in us-west-2 using our internal test harness and the exact headers they supplied.
- Pulled server logs for the provided request ids window (no exact matches in logs; I checked account-scoped tails).

Findings
- The platform returned normal 200 responses in our tests; we also observed a small number of short-stream events from an older client pattern where the client closed the TCP stream early.
- For the request ids they sent we do not have entry logs showing server-side exceptions or 5xxs for their account during the reported timeframe. All platform-side traces for nearby timestamps are typical (healthy token throughput, no kernel crashes).

Root cause hypothesis
- The customer's SDK (v1.3.0) appears to have a known edge-case in streaming handling where very small content-lengths combined with connection pooling can surface as an empty payload on the client side (we have an internal note referencing this behavior). The bug was addressed in SDK v1.4.2 (fix: ensure proper stream drain before connection reuse).

Action taken
- Generated a support log (redwood_support_log_60811.txt) with the server-side tails we captured and the harness replay details.
- Verified that replaying their payloads with the patched SDK returns consistent non-empty outputs.

Conclusion
- No evidence of a platform-side bug. Likely client-side SDK edge-case (stream handling). Recommended next step: customer upgrade to Redwood JS SDK v1.4.2 and retest. If they still see empty bodies after upgrade, we'll escalate to an infra kernel deep-dive.

Connor O'Brien
Platform Support Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Lucas Perry <lucas@cascade.ai>
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Unexpected missing answers from Redwood endpoint — summary and recommended remediation

Hi Lucas — thanks again for the report and for providing the traces. We completed an initial triage:

Summary
- Redwood platform logs show no server-side errors or 5xx events correlated to the request window you provided.
- Our reproductions indicate the issue is most consistent with an edge-case in the Redwood JS SDK v1.3.0 streaming/connection reuse logic.

Recommended next steps
1) Please upgrade to Redwood JS SDK v1.4.2 (contains a streaming drain fix) and re-run the failing job.
2) If you still see empty responses, capture one full raw request/response (including headers) and share the request id — we'll do an immediate deep-dive.

We've attached the support log we generated (redwood_support_log_60811.txt) and a short replay summary. As a gesture for the production interruption we can apply a 10k token service credit to your account; let me know if that helps.

If you'd like, Connor can run a timed replay with you on a quick call.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Support | Redwood Inference
